directions.name: Liman
directions.reference: A port's bill of lading and container stowage plan: printed forms on off-white paper, stamped in one ink, read by people checking codes line by line.
directions.summary: Operational and calm: port-paperwork neutrals, container green for actions, signal amber for attention.
directions.audience: Warehouse staff and SME owners tracking dozens of shipments a day, often on a phone.
rationale: Illustrative: in this example the competitor scan found blue and red accents, so green is a free hue in the category.
Atkinson Hyperlegible Next keeps tracking codes and addresses unambiguous for warehouse staff.
Schibsted Grotesk has the compact, label-like headlines of freight documents without looking like a template.

type_notes.heading: compact grotesque with the feel of printed freight forms
type_notes.body: distinct I/l/1 and 0/O for addresses and tracking codes

donts: Don't use rounded, friendly illustration; this is paperwork, not a consumer app.

directions.name: Konteyner
directions.reference: Stenciled lettering on corten-steel shipping containers and the numbered bay signs of a container yard.
directions.summary: Industrial and confident: steel greys with container-red actions and heavy, compact headlines.
directions.audience: Logistics managers comparing carriers and costs on desktop.
rationale: Container red is recognizable on a warehouse floor and differs from the category's blue default.
Chivo at heavy weights gives stencil-like authority; Public Sans keeps dense tables readable.

type_notes.heading: heavy, compact grotesque that reads like stenciled bay numbers
type_notes.body: neutral grotesque that holds up in dense tables

directions.name: Rıhtım
directions.reference: A shipping line's printed timetable and stamped parcel labels: slab-serif headings, one ink blue, plain paper.
directions.summary: Editorial and trustworthy: ink blue on plain paper, slab headlines like shipping labels.
directions.audience: Customers checking where their parcel is, mostly on mobile.
rationale: Zilla Slab echoes stamped shipping labels; Hanken Grotesk keeps UI copy neutral.
Ink blue is used as text-weight color, not as a glowing brand fill, so it reads as print rather than SaaS.

type_notes.heading: slab serif with the weight of a rubber stamp
